Select the best clustered strain of each cluster

Source: R/select_silhouette.R
select_silhouette.Rd

Cuts the strains into k clusters with factoextra::hcut() and selects, in each cluster, the strain with the largest silhouette width. When several strains share the largest silhouette width, one of them is chosen at random.

Usage

select_silhouette(
  prepared_data,
  dist,
  k,
  isdiss = inherits(dist, "dist"),
  hc_func = "hclust",
  hc_method = "complete",
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

prepared_data

A data frame with one row per strain, as returned by prepare_input(). Its rows must be in the same order as in dist.

dist

A dissimilarity object, e.g. gower_dist returned by assess_gower().

k

Number of clusters, i.e. number of strains to select. Must be between 2 and the number of strains minus 1.

isdiss

Logical, whether dist is a dissimilarity object (default: TRUE when dist inherits from "dist").

hc_func

Hierarchical clustering function passed to factoextra::hcut(): "hclust" (default), "agnes" or "diana".

hc_method

Agglomeration method passed to factoextra::hcut(), "complete" by default.

seed

An integer passed to set.seed() to make the choice between ex aequo strains reproducible, or NULL (default) to leave the random number generator untouched.

Value

prepared_data with three additional columns:

cluster

the cluster of the strain;

size

the number of strains in this cluster;

selected

the identifier of the strain selected for this cluster.

The selected strains are given by unique(result$selected).

See also

Other clustering method: assess_gower(), cstats_table(), export_selection(), report_selection(), select_strains()

Examples

raw_data <- salmonella_strains
prepared_data <- prepare_input(raw_data, col_select = c("CONTEXTE", "MATRICE1", "REGION", "SECTEUR", "LIEUPVT"),
                               id = "IDENTIFIANT", date = "DATE_PRELEVEMENT")
#> no duplicate ID
#> selected metadata: CONTEXTE, MATRICE1, REGION, SECTEUR, LIEUPVT, ANNEE
gower <- assess_gower(prepared_data, graph = FALSE)
selection <- select_silhouette(prepared_data, dist = gower$gower_dist, k = 20,
                               seed = 1)
# the 20 strains to sequence
unique(selection$selected)
#>  [1] "2020LSAL00802" "2020LSAL00487" "2020LSAL00177" "2020LSAL00854"
#>  [5] "2020LSAL00454" "2020LSAL00720" "2020LSAL00506" "2020LSAL00550"
#>  [9] "2020LSAL00660" "2020LSAL00668" "2020LSAL00724" "2020LSAL00790"
#> [13] "2020LSAL00912" "2020LSAL00792" "2020LSAL00866" "2020LSAL00892"
#> [17] "2020LSAL01016" "2020LSAL00994" "2020LSAL01040" "2020LSAL01188"
